1.s: Paul prays for the Colossians and praises Christ: “the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of all creation… all things have been created through him and for him… in him all things are held together.”
1.d: “He is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of all creation” [[bible:Colossians 1:15]]. 1:15–20 probably quotes an early Christian hymn about Jesus as creator and redeemer [[tosn:Colossians 1:15-20]]: all things were made through him and for him [[tosn:Colossians 1:16]].

2.s: In Christ “all the fullness of the Deity dwells bodily.” Don’t be taken captive by empty philosophy, rules about food and festivals, or the worship of angels.
2.d: “Triumphing over them” pictures a Roman victory parade: through the cross God has defeated the spiritual powers [[tosn:Colossians 2:15]], and those who died with Christ are set free from them [[tosn:Colossians 2:20]].

3.s: “Set your mind on the things that are above.” Put off anger and lies; put on compassion, kindness and love. “Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly.” Household relationships.
3.d: “Barbarian, Scythian”: Greeks mocked other peoples who could not speak Greek well, yet in Christ “Christ is all, and in all” [[tosn:Colossians 3:11]] [[bible:Colossians 3:11]]. Slave or free, every Christian serves the Lord Christ [[tosn:Colossians 3:22-24]].

4.s: Devote yourselves to prayer; let your speech be gracious. Greetings, including from Luke, “the beloved physician”, and Mark.
4.d: Paul asks that “the letter from Laodicea” be read too [[bible:Colossians 4:16]]. People have tried to match it with a New Testament letter, but it has probably been lost [[tosn:Colossians 4:16]]. Tychicus probably carried this letter along with Ephesians and Philemon [[tosn:Colossians 4:7]].
